summary: These tables report institution-level enrollment and instructional activity for the full July 1, 2020–June 30, 2021 reporting period, covering students and activity at any time during the year rather than a single census date. The universe is IPEDS postsecondary institutions reporting applicable undergraduate and/or graduate activity; measures are reported by institution and student level, with unduplicated enrollment used where headcounts are shown. The 12-month measure is especially useful for institutions with nontraditional calendars or short-term programs.

Completions is an annual collection covering awards conferred from July 1, 2020, through June 30, 2021. It reports at the institution, program, and award-level record level for eligible IPEDS postsecondary institutions that grant certificates or degrees, with counts of awards, recipients, or programs depending on the table. The survey uses the applicable CIP classification and includes only completions and program offerings associated with that reporting period.

Fall Enrollment reports institution-level student counts for the fall reporting period. Traditional academic-year institutions report as of October 15 or their official fall reporting date, while institutions with program-based or continuous calendars report students enrolled at any time from August 1 through October 31. Institutions can have multiple records, with each record representing a defined student subgroup; table-specific eligibility and optional or unavailable collections apply.

Finance is collected annually during the winter collection period for the most recently completed fiscal year, covering the fiscal year ending between July 1, 2020, and June 30, 2021. The unit of observation is the institution (one record per UNITID), and the universe is postsecondary institutions eligible and required to report IPEDS finance data, with reporting form determined by sector and accounting standards. Financial measures are reported under separate accounting models, so public GASB, FASB, and private for-profit records should be queried from their applicable tables rather than treated as interchangeable.

Graduation Rates reports institution-level outcomes for cohorts of full-time, first-time, degree- or certificate-seeking undergraduates, tracking enrollment and completion or transfer status at specified points within normal time. The 2021 collection reports status as of August 31, 2021, using cohort records and completion windows of 100%, 150%, or 200% of normal time. Coverage varies by institutional sector and cohort, so the applicable table must be selected based on whether the institution is four-year, two-year, or less-than-two-year and on the outcome window needed.

Human Resources data describe staff at institutions in the IPEDS reporting universe, using UNITID as the institution identifier and allowing multiple records per institution by staff category or other dimensions. Fall staff counts are reported for the November 1, 2021 payroll snapshot; salary tables cover academic year 2021-22, and new-hire tables cover the applicable prior-year hiring period. Some tables impose narrower eligibility rules, especially degree-granting institutions with at least 15 full-time employees and related administrative offices.

Institutional Characteristics covers the 2021-22 IPEDS universe and is collected through the fall, winter, and spring reporting components, with some fields updated from later admissions, enrollment, and library collections. The universe is active postsecondary institutions in IPEDS; Title IV institutions for which IPEDS reporting is mandatory are included, although applicability varies by institution and some institutions report for multiple campuses. Most data are institution-level, with specialized records for branch locations and custom comparison-group members.

These institution-level reports cover student aid and benefits received during the academic year, July 1, 2020 through June 30, 2021, for postsecondary institutions eligible to participate in federal Title IV programs. The unit of observation is the institution, with counts and dollar amounts aggregated for specified student populations rather than individual student records; eligibility and population definitions vary by table, and the component includes both undergraduate and graduate students where specified.
